metadata.description: Major Muharram and Safar processions (jaloos) in Pakistan, compiled from official traffic advisories and police reports
metadata.note: Routes and dates may change every year. Google Maps links are based on starting point names. Always confirm locally.

processions.name: Pandu Street Procession
processions.description: One of the three major processions held on the 9th of Muharram in Lahore. It begins from Pandu Street in Islampura and proceeds through Siraj Building, Islampura Chowk, and Neeli Bagh Chowk towards old Anarkali. The procession reaches Khaima-e-Sadaat via Old Anarkali, AG Office, and Baba Mauj Darya Road, where a mourning gathering and Maghrib prayers are held. It then returns along its designated route and concludes back at Pandu Street. Anti-smog guns and sprinklers are used along the route to provide relief from the intense heat.
processions.notes: One of six major processions on 9th Muharram

processions.name: Qasr-e-Batool Procession
processions.description: The third major procession of 9th Muharram in Lahore, originating from Qasr-e-Batool in the Shadman area. It is one of six major processions scheduled for the 9th of Muharram across the city, as confirmed by the Chief Traffic Officer's route inspection. The procession route extends from Shadman to Shah Jamal.
processions.notes: Third major procession on 9th Muharram

processions.name: Central Zuljanah Procession
processions.description: The most important Ashura procession in Lahore, beginning from Nisar Haveli inside Mochi Gate on the night between 9th and 10th Muharram. It follows a centuries-old traditional route through the Walled City, passing numerous historic Imambargahs, mosques, and bazaars including Mohalla Chehl Bibian, Mubarik Haveli, Chowk Nawab Sahib, Kashmiri Bazaar, Sunehri Mosque, Dabbi Bazaar, Gumti Bazaar, and Bhaati Chowk. The procession concludes at Karbala Gamay Shah around 8:00 pm on 10th Muharram. After its conclusion, Shaam-e-Ghariban is observed, where religious scholars highlight the martyrdom of Imam Hussain and his companions. The procession is monitored by over 395 CCTV cameras, with snipers deployed on rooftops and more than 11,000 police officers on security duty.
processions.notes: The most important Ashura procession in Lahore. It follows a traditional route through the old city and ends at Karbala Gamay Shah.

processions.name: Lal Pul Nabi Pura Zuljanah
processions.description: One of several Zuljanah processions taken out from different neighbourhoods of Lahore on 10th Muharram. These smaller processions allow mourners from various areas to participate in azadari without travelling to the central route.
processions.notes: One of the Zuljanah processions

processions.name: Model Town Zuljanah
processions.description: A neighbourhood Zuljanah procession from Model Town, one of the designated areas for 10th Muharram processions in Lahore. These local processions complement the central Ashura procession and allow residents of Model Town and surrounding areas to participate in the commemoration.
processions.notes: One of the Zuljanah processions

processions.name: Chung Zuljanah
processions.description: A Zuljanah procession from the Chung area, reflecting the spread of Muharram observances across Lahore's expanding urban boundaries. It is one of the designated locations for local processions on 10th Muharram.
processions.notes: One of the Zuljanah processions

processions.name: Thokar Niaz Baig Zuljanah
processions.description: A Zuljanah procession from Thokar Niaz Baig, one of the designated locations for local processions on 10th Muharram in Lahore. SPAL sanitation teams perform cleaning duties along the procession route in Thokar village.
processions.notes: One of the Zuljanah processions

processions.name: Chehlum Central Procession
processions.description: The main Chehlum procession on 20th Safar, marking forty days after Ashura. It begins from Haveli Alif Shah near Delhi Gate and concludes at Karbala Gamay Shah, passing through traditional routes. A total of 12 processions are held across Lahore on this day. Security is provided for 44 gatherings and 17 processions, with over 10,000 officers deployed, 390 walk-through gates, and 6,427 metal detectors. Female police personnel perform checking duties for women mourners. Traffic is diverted from 19 locations across the city to facilitate mourners.
processions.notes: Main Chehlum procession on 20th Safar. A total of 12 processions are held in the city on this day.

processions.name: Central 9th Muharram Procession
processions.description: The main procession of 9th Muharram in Islamabad, taken out from Imambargah G-6/2 in the afternoon. The Islamabad Capital Territory Police and Islamabad Traffic Police make elaborate security arrangements, with more than a thousand officials deployed to ensure security and smooth traffic flow. A Central Control Room at Safe City monitors the procession. The procession follows its designated route through the G-6 sector before returning to the starting point.
processions.notes: Main procession of 9th Muharram in the federal capital

processions.name: Central Ashura Procession
processions.end: Markazi Isna Ashari Imambargah, G-6/2 (returns to starting point)
processions.description: The central Ashura procession in Islamabad, taken out after Zuhr prayers from Markazi Isna Ashari Imambargah in G-6/2. The procession passes through its designated route and culminates at the same place later in the night. For security, pillion riding is banned on 9th and 10th Muharram, and a seven-layer security programme is implemented with Safe City and drone camera surveillance. A total of 181 processions and 965 Majalis are scheduled citywide during Muharram, requiring the deployment of over 16,000 police and Rangers personnel.
processions.notes: Central Ashura procession. Pillion riding banned on 9th and 10th Muharram

processions.name: I-10/1 Zuljanah Procession
processions.end: Imambargah Musa Kazim (returns to starting point)
processions.route: Street No. I-10/1, Khayaban-e-Sir Syed, CDA Double Road
processions.description: A 10th Muharram procession in Sector I-10, commencing from Imambargah Musa Kazim and proceeding through Street No. I-10/1, Khayaban-e-Sir Syed, and CDA Double Road before concluding at the same Imambargah. The Islamabad Traffic Police issues a diversion plan for this procession, with roads including Street No. 18, CDA Chowk, and service roads closed or diverted. Commuters are advised to use alternate routes including I-10 Markaz Service Road, IJP Road, and Pirwadhai Hill Road.
processions.notes: Procession in Sector I-10 with traffic diversion plan

processions.name: F-11/3 Zuljanah Procession
processions.start: House No. 366, Street No. 37, Sector F-11/3
processions.description: A 10th Muharram procession beginning at 12:00 noon from House No. 366, Street No. 37, Sector F-11/3. The Islamabad Traffic Police issues a diversion plan, with traffic diverted at F-11/2 Signal, F-11 Double Road, Naval Colony, Hilal Road, near Haidri Chowk, Beaconhouse School, and Telenor Plaza. Commuters are advised to use alternate routes including Service Road (Maira Abadi), Kazmin Chowk, F-10/1 Haidri Chowk corner, and Margalla Road.
processions.notes: Procession in Sector F-11 with traffic diversion plan

processions.name: Shah Allah Ditta Procession
processions.start: Residence of Mushtaq Shah, Shah Allah Ditta
processions.description: A mourning procession on 11th Muharram in the Shah Allah Ditta area of Islamabad. The Chief Traffic Officer visits the Shah Allah Ditta procession route to review traffic and security arrangements, directing officers to ensure smooth traffic flow and facilitate mourners while strictly implementing the approved traffic management plan.
processions.notes: Procession on 11th Muharram in Shah Allah Ditta area

processions.name: Bari Imam Procession
processions.description: A major mourning procession on 11th Muharram travelling from Purana Imambargah Noor Pur Shahan to the Bari Imam Shrine. The Chief Traffic Officer visits the Bari Imam procession route to review arrangements and ensure effective traffic management. The 11th Muharram observances continue the commemoration of Karbala after the intensity of Ashura.
processions.notes: Main procession on 11th Muharram to Bari Imam Shrine

processions.name: 24th Muharram Procession
processions.end: Imambargah Boota Sain Darbar (Islamabad Expressway green belt)
processions.description: A procession on 24th Muharram that begins from Rawalpindi and concludes near the Islamabad Expressway green belt. This reflects the continuation of mourning observances throughout the month of Muharram, not just the first ten days.
processions.notes: Starts from Rawalpindi and ends near Islamabad Expressway

processions.name: Chehlum Central Procession
processions.description: The central Chehlum procession in Islamabad on 20th Safar, marking forty days after Ashura. It concludes at Imambargah Asna Ashari in Sector G-6. Federal ministers inspect security preparations in the G-6 sector, focusing on the central Imambargah Asna Ashari and procession routes. Officials brief them on comprehensive security measures including surveillance through the Safe City Islamabad Control Room.
processions.notes: Central Chehlum procession concluding at Imambargah Asna Ashari, G-6

processions.name: 6th Muharram Procession
processions.route: Street No. 6, Old Airport Road, PAF Chowk
processions.description: The first major mourning procession of Muharram in Rawalpindi, commencing from Gulzar Hussain Shah Street No. 9 and proceeding through Street No. 6, Old Airport Road, and PAF Chowk before concluding at Imambargah Isna Asharia in Gracy Line. More than 50 traffic police personnel are deployed along the route and at diversion points. Traffic from Koral Chowk towards Ammar Chowk is diverted via the National Bank U-turn, where two-way traffic is maintained.
processions.notes: More than 50 traffic police personnel deployed. Parking banned along route.

processions.name: 7th Muharram Central Procession
processions.route: Transformer Chowk, Kuri Road, Chah Sultan, Glass Factory Chowk, Zafarul Haq Road, Leprosy Hospital, Murree Road, Committee Chowk, Iqbal Road, Naya Mohalla Chowk, Fawara Chowk, Jamia Masjid Road
processions.description: The 7th Muharram procession begins after Maghrib prayers from Nishtar Street in Sadiqabad and follows a long traditional route through Rawalpindi, uniting with other processions at Naya Mohalla Chowk before culminating at Imambargah Qadim via Fawara Chowk and Jamia Masjid Road. More than 225 traffic police personnel are deployed. Diversion points are strictly sealed with barriers, and roads are reopened in phases as the procession advances.
processions.notes: More than 225 traffic police personnel deployed. Diversion points sealed with barriers.

processions.name: 9th Muharram Central Procession
processions.route: Traditional route through old city areas
processions.description: The central 9th Muharram procession in Rawalpindi begins from the historic Chittian Hattian area and follows its traditional route before concluding at Colonel Maqbool Imambargah. Markets remain closed along the route, snipers are stationed at sensitive locations, and police, Rangers, and other security agencies maintain a heavy presence. A total of 350 CCTV cameras are installed along procession routes. The stretch from Fawara Chowk to Dingi Khoi Chowk is declared highly sensitive, with Rangers deployed in surrounding areas.
processions.notes: Snipers stationed at sensitive locations. Fawara Chowk to Dingi Khoi Chowk highly sensitive.

processions.name: Ashura Central Processions (6 processions)
processions.type: Central Zuljanah, Alam, Tazia, Jhoola, Mehndi
processions.description: On Youm-e-Ashura, six central processions featuring Zuljanah, Alam, Tazia, Jhoola, and Mehndi are taken out across Rawalpindi. More than 1,100 traffic officers and personnel are deployed citywide. Key traffic restrictions include: all traffic prohibited from entering Iqbal Road from Committee Chowk; traffic access to College Road and Fawara Chowk restricted due to diversions at DAV College Chowk; traffic at City Saddar Road's Mashriq Hotel diversion point redirected towards Saddar and Mohanpura; traffic heading towards Kashmiri Bazaar not permitted from Cinema Chowk; complete diversions at Banni Chowk with traffic routed through Circular Road and Kohati Bazaar; diversions at Hamilton Chowk and Banswala Chowk; at Pir Choha Chowk, traffic access towards Imambargah Baltistania blocked. For the Satellite Town procession, diversions implemented on both sides of Imambargah Yadgar Hussaini.
processions.notes: Six central processions. More than 1,100 traffic officers deployed. Citizens advised to avoid unnecessary travel towards Raja Bazaar.

processions.name: 11th Muharram Peshawar Road Procession
processions.description: A mourning procession on 11th Muharram in the Peshawar Road area, continuing observances after Ashura. Under the traffic management plan, the road from Charing Cross to Pirwadhai Mor remains completely closed. Traffic heading from Saddar to Peshawar is diverted via Westridge, while vehicles travelling from Peshawar to Saddar are allowed to enter through Carriage Factory Road. Misrial Road remains closed from Chohar Chowk to Range Chowk, with traffic approaching Chohar Chowk from Misrial Road diverted to Range Road. Hali Road remains closed from Chohar Chowk to Najam Shaheed Chowk, with traffic from Marble Factory Road redirected towards Westridge Road. Allahabad Road remains closed from Ashiana Chowk to Progressive School.
processions.notes: Peshawar Road, ABL Street, Misrial Road, and Hali Road closed during procession.

processions.name: 5th Muharram Evening Procession
processions.description: An evening procession on 5th Muharram, with roads closed from Daulat Gate Chowk to Darbar Shah Shams. Haram Gate, Bohar Gate Alang, Pak Gate, Khooni Bridge, and Pul Shidi Lal to Lal Road are also closed to traffic. Sadar Bazaar Cantt remains closed in the evening. Alternative routes include Hafiz Jamal Road, Masoom Shah Road, Kabutar Mandi, Quaid-e-Azam Road, and Qasim Road.
processions.notes: Evening procession. Roads closed from Daulat Gate Chowk to Darbar Shah Shams.

processions.name: 6th Muharram Traditional Mourning Procession
processions.start: Residence of Makhdoom Pir Syed Kazim Ali Shah
processions.end: Astana Aaliya Makhdoom Syed Amir Shah Bukhari, Thala Saadat
processions.description: An ancient traditional mourning procession on 6th Muharram, led by Makhdoom Pir Syed Qaisar Abbas Shah Bukhari. The procession follows its historic route and concludes at Astana Aaliya Makhdoom Syed Amir Shah Bukhari in Thala Saadat. Administrative duties are performed by Syed Musa Raza Bukhari, Central President of the Licensed Organizers Organization. Multan Metro Bus Service remains fully suspended on this day.
processions.notes: Ancient traditional procession. Metro Bus Service suspended.

processions.name: 9th Muharram Central Procession
processions.description: The central 9th Muharram mourning procession in Multan, emerging from Mumtazabad Imambargah. Numerous processions of Alam and Zuljanah are taken out from different areas of the city under a three-layer security shield, with heavy contingents deployed on all routes. Authorities monitor the route through CCTV surveillance and drones, with Safe City Multan Control Room conducting round-the-clock monitoring.
processions.notes: Central procession from Mumtazabad Imambargah. Three-layer security shield.

processions.name: Ashura Processions
processions.description: On Youm-e-Ashura, mourning processions are held across Multan Division. A total of 224 majalis and 283 processions are held across Multan Division, with all sensitive gatherings linked to the Safe City surveillance system. More than 13,000 security personnel are deployed to maintain peace. CCTV cameras are installed at all key locations, with representatives of all relevant departments present in the District Control Room for coordinated monitoring. Punjab Education Minister visits Ashura processions at Ghanta Ghar Chowk and Haram Gate.
processions.notes: 224 majalis and 283 processions across Multan Division. More than 13,000 security personnel deployed.

processions.name: Chehlum Central Procession
processions.description: The main Chehlum procession on 20th Safar in Multan, beginning from Hussain Agahi Bazaar. More than 300 traffic officers and personnel are deployed to ensure smooth traffic flow and facilitate mourners. Roads closed during the procession include Hussain Agahi Bazaar, Hussain Agahi Chowk to Ghanta Ghar Chowk, Ghanta Ghar Chowk to Kachehri Chowk, Gur Mandi, Chowk Bazaar, inside Hussain Agahi, and inside Bohar Gate Road. CPO Sadiq Ali Dogar holds consultation meetings with licensed organizers and traders' representatives for peaceful observance. Search operations continue in and around procession routes, with technical sweeping conducted before processions begin.
processions.notes: Main Chehlum procession from Hussain Agahi Bazaar. More than 300 traffic officers deployed.

processions.name: Faisalabad Division overview (1st-10th Muharram)
processions.description: 1,528 processions and 4,402 Majalis across Faisalabad Division during the first 10 days of Muharram. On 9th and 10th Muharram specifically: 246 processions and 163 Majalis in Faisalabad district, with more than 8,000 police and security personnel deployed (more than 15,000 across the Division for the full 10 days). The central area is Clock Tower (Ghanta Ghar) and the Central Imambargah area. Detailed route-wise procession lists are not publicly available; only aggregate data and road closure information are provided.
processions.notes: Helpline 1915 available for traffic assistance

processions.name: Ashura day road closures
processions.route: Chiniot Bazaar Chowk to Chenab Chowk; Jhang Bazaar entrance to Kothi Tahir Shah; Chiniot Bazaar Chowk to Gumti Chowk; Gumti Chowk to Karkhana Bazaar entrance; Salemi Chowk to Jhal Chowk; GTS Chowk to District Council Chowk; District Council Chowk to Kutchery Bazaar Chowk; Eidgah Chowk to Kotwali Chowk; Nishat Cinema Chowk to Narwala Road
processions.description: On 10th Muharram (Ashura), the listed roads are completely closed to general traffic. The central procession route passes through the Clock Tower area and Central Imambargah. Alternative routes for commuters: Rajbah Road, Janab Chowk, and Jhang Road to Jail Road.
processions.notes: Helpline 1915 available for traffic assistance

processions.name: Continuous closures (1st-10th Muharram)
processions.route: Chenab Chowk to Kotwali Chowk; Kotwali Chowk to Narwala Imambargah Road; Narwala Chowk to Central Imambargah Road; Kothi Tahir Shah to Central Imambargah Road; Jame Masjid Anwari to Central Imambargah Road
processions.description: These roads remain closed from the beginning of Muharram until the 10th, as they form the core route for processions and Majalis around the Central Imambargah area. The closures facilitate mourners and ensure security for gatherings.
processions.notes: Continuous closure from 1st to 10th Muharram

processions.name: Central Ashura Procession
processions.description: The central Ashura procession in Faisalabad, originating from the Central Imambargah area near Clock Tower. It is the largest procession in the city, with extensive security arrangements including CCTV monitoring, drone surveillance, and deployment of over 8,000 police personnel. The route is closed to general traffic, and mourners participate in matam and noha khwani along the way. Nine licensed organizers coordinate with authorities for peaceful observance.
processions.notes: Largest procession in Faisalabad. Central Imambargah area.

processions.name: 9th Muharram Processions
processions.description: Multiple processions are held across Faisalabad on 9th Muharram. A total of 246 processions and 163 Majalis are held in the district on 9th and 10th Muharram combined, with more than 8,000 security personnel deployed. The city's main procession routes converge around the Clock Tower and Central Imambargah area.
processions.notes: Part of 246 processions held on 9th and 10th Muharram

processions.name: Chehlum Procession
processions.description: Faisalabad is one of 18 districts in Punjab where Chehlum (20th Safar) processions are held under heightened security. Pakistan Army and Rangers assist police in maintaining security. Specific procession routes are not publicly detailed in available advisories. Mourners observe Chehlum to mark forty days after Ashura, with Majalis and processions held across the city.
processions.notes: Part of Punjab-wide Chehlum security deployment. Army and Rangers assistance.
